name: Wisconsin Wetland Conservation Trust: Restore (wetland restoration grants)

funder.name: Wisconsin Department of Natural Resources (Wisconsin Wetland Conservation Trust)

summary: In-lieu-fee funding for wetland restoration projects on permanent mitigation sites in Wisconsin, with quarterly proposal windows. Nonprofit conservation organisations can apply, and a separate strand covers nonprofit projects on DNR-owned or eased lands.

steps: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers review, if selected

eligibility.rule: Project site is protected in perpetuity by a conservation easement or comparable legal instrument
Project site is in a service area with currently available funding
No research, education and outreach, or upland preservation except eligible upland buffers
For preservation credit, site has high ecological quality and an imminent threat of destruction or invasion

documents: Applicant qualifications, if the applicant implements the project
Applicant wetland mitigation project list for the last 10 years, if implementing the project
Contractor or consultant qualifications, if hired to implement the project
Contractor or consultant wetland restoration project list for the last 10 years, if hired
DNR Property Manager support letter, for State Lands applicants
Proof the project is on Department land, for State Lands applicants
Proof of 501(c)(3) status, for State Lands applicants

applicant_types.quote: Open to all public agencies, municipalities, private landowners, environmental consultants, nonprofit conservation organizations, Wisconsin tribes, or any entity registered with the Wisconsin Department of Financial Institutions.

geography.quote: Projects may be completed on any lands in the state of Wisconsin

access.quote: Applications will only be accepted using the 'Submit by email...' button and the corresponding instructions described on page 1 of the WWCT Grant Application.

window.quote: Proposals are reviewed on a rolling quarterly basis, with deadlines for submittal one month before the end of each quarter.

effort.quote: The current Request for Proposal (RFP) is open on September 1, 2026, with a deadline on October 31, 2026.
Proposals are reviewed on a rolling quarterly basis, with deadlines for submittal one month before the end of each quarter.
Selected proposals are generally subject to U.S. Army Corps of Engineers review prior to the creation of a WWCT contract for the project.
The WWCT works with project proponent to develop Final Prospectus to submit to the Corps/IRT.

eligibility.quote: all project sites must be protected by a conservation easement or comparable legal instrument and remain as a mitigation site in perpetuity.
To be selected, project proposal sites must fall within a service area with currently available funding.
Prohibited funding uses include: research, education and outreach, and upland preservation (besides eligible upland buffers).
For preservation credit, sites must have high ecological quality under demonstrable imminent threat of destruction from development or invasion

after_award.quote: Monitoring reports are due to the WWCT by November 1 of each monitoring year.
Site visits with the WWCT and the Corps/IRT will be scheduled as needed throughout the project design, construction, and monitoring phases.

documents.quote: If the applicant plans to be the primary party implementing the project, they must provide qualifications and a list of wetland mitigation projects completed within the last 10 years.

If an applicant plans to hire professional contractors or consultants to implement the project, then they must provide the contractor or consultant's qualifications and a list of wetland restoration projects completed within the last 10 years.

Applicants for the State Lands Grant Subprogram are required to discuss their project with the DNR Property Manager at the proposed site and to submit a letter of support from them with the application.

Applicants seeking to apply for funds through the State Lands Grant Subprogram must provide documentation showing that their proposed project is located on Department land (as defined in s. 23.09(2)(d), Wis. Stats.), and has been endorsed by the local DNR property manager. Applicants must also provide proof of their 501(c)(3) status.
